titleZh: 某個角色本來就包含的事

brief.meaningEn: Be an expected part of a particular activity, situation or role.
brief.meaningZh: 是某活動、情況或角色中可預期的一部分。
brief.grammar: questions/changes come with the territory; came in past; identify the role or situation that makes them expected.
brief.register: Established territory metaphor. It explains an expected feature without necessarily approving of it or making it unlimited.
brief.boundaryZh: 常見或可預期不等於任何要求都合理、沒有界線或不能改善；要交代實際責任。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可預先準備常見問題，也可明確說哪些要求不屬約定範圍。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述角色的常見需要，分清預期、同意及無限義務。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Some late calls come with the territory in emergency work.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 22, table 1, row 8; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Last-minute room questions come with the territory when I staff the welcome desk, so I keep the current plan nearby; requests to change the programme still go to the organiser.
listening.zh: 負責接待櫃檯時，最後一刻問房間是可預期部分，所以我把最新圖留身旁；改節目請求仍交主辦者。
listening.promptZh: 哪些是角色預期工作，哪些另有負責人？

options.en: Room questions are expected at the desk; programme changes remain with the organiser.
options.zh: 櫃檯預期答房間問題；改節目仍屬主辦者。

options.en: The desk volunteer handles programme changes as well as room questions.
options.zh: 櫃檯義工除房間問題，也負責節目改動。

options.en: Room questions are normally referred to the organiser rather than answered at the desk.
options.zh: 房間問題通常轉主辦者，而非櫃檯回答。

options.en: The organiser has already transferred programme decisions to the desk.
options.zh: 主辦者已把節目決策交櫃檯。

listening.explanationZh: 角色常見問題可準備，still organiser限定決策範圍。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把最新房間圖放身旁？
reply.promptEn: Why do you keep the current room plan nearby?

options.en: People often ask room questions at the welcome desk.
options.zh: 接待櫃檯常有人問房間。

options.en: Those questions come with the territory when I staff the desk.
options.zh: 負責櫃檯時，那些問題本來就可預期。

options.en: The plan helps me respond to a normal part of the role.
options.zh: 圖幫我回應角色常見工作。

options.en: Answering location questions is part of what visitors need from the desk.
options.zh: 答地點問題是訪客需櫃檯提供的部分。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給角色需要，不擴成所有決定。

scene.promptZh: 你帶第一次來的訪客看展，經常需重講指路，已準備簡短說明；特殊活動申請仍由主管答。哪句準確？

options.en: Repeating directions comes with the territory when guiding first-time visitors.
options.zh: 帶初訪者時，重講指路是角色可預期部分。

options.en: Guiding visitors also gives me authority to approve special event requests.
options.zh: 帶訪客也讓我有權批准特殊活動請求。

options.en: The directions are normally provided only after the supervisor has approved an event request.
options.zh: 通常要主管先批准活動請求，才提供指路。

scene.explanationZh: 初訪者常需重講指路，但特殊活動申請仍由主管回答；指路與申請批准不能混為同一責任或前後條件。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 comes with the territory 得出？

options.en: Something is an expected part of the situation.
options.zh: 某事是情況中可預期部分。

options.en: The role has no limits and any request must be accepted.
options.zh: 角色沒有界線，任何請求都必須接受。

options.en: The context should explain which role is involved.
options.zh: 情境應解釋涉及哪角色。

contrast.explanationZh: 可預期不等於無限義務。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「既然有人會問改節目，你也應直接批嗎？」但你的工作只是櫃檯指路。哪句最好？

options.en: Questions may arise, but programme changes still need the organiser’s decision.
options.zh: 問題可能出現，但改節目仍需主辦者決定。

options.en: Yes, receiving a request gives me the authority to approve it.
options.zh: 對，收到請求就讓我有權批准。

options.en: Should I send even the ordinary room questions to the organiser along with the programme requests?
options.zh: 我應否把一般房間問題也與節目請求一起轉主辦者？

dialogue.explanationZh: 櫃檯可答一般指路，節目改動交負責人；不要把接問題當授權，也不要把自己可答的問題全部轉走。

speaking.en: Questions come with the territory, but I should know which decisions belong to someone else.
speaking.zh: 問題是角色可預期部分，但我應知道哪些決定屬別人。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清預期與權責。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你接受替社團編月訊，知道截稿前常有人補照片或問字數，想預先寫清可補資料的時限，過期改下一期；你不想承諾任何時間都重排整份。用一至兩句英文向投稿者說明。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以截稿前補問的常見需要說明角色預期，提出清楚時限及下一期安排，不把可預期變任何時候都需全改。

examples.en: Late questions come with the territory when editing the newsletter, so I will state a clear deadline for extra photographs. Material arriving later can go into the next issue.
examples.zh: 編月訊時，遲來問題本來可預期，所以我會列清補照片期限。較後材料可放下一期。

examples.en: I know changes come with the territory, but we need an agreed cutoff for this issue. That will help contributors know what can still be included.
examples.zh: 我知改動是角色可預期部分，但本期需議定截止點。這會幫投稿者知道仍可加甚麼。

takeaways.en: Unexpected questions came with the territory when she led the first-time visitors.
takeaways.zh: 帶初訪者時，意料外問題是角色可預期部分。

takeaways.en: Some revisions come with the territory, so we left time to discuss them before printing.
takeaways.zh: 有些修訂本來可預期，所以印前我們留時間討論。

brief.meaningEn: Something regarded as a sign of pride, achievement or status.
brief.meaningZh: 某事被視為自豪、成就或地位的標記。
brief.grammar: treat/see something as a badge of honour; it is/is not a badge of honour; British honour spelling retained.
brief.register: Established insignia metaphor. It reports how something is valued, not necessarily whether that judgement is justified.
brief.boundaryZh: 被視為自豪標記，不代表正式獎章、客觀最好或說話者必認同；可批評某種不當自豪。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需分清人物感到自豪及事實效果，不把帶傷疲累等狀態自動當成就。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述某行動被怎樣賦予地位，並保留評價立場。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Working without rest should not be a badge of honour.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 22, table 1, row 9; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: He treated doing the whole project alone as a badge of honour, but the missed checks showed why the team needed to share the work rather than admire the workload.
listening.zh: 他把整項獨做當自豪標記，但漏核顯示團隊需分工，而非只崇拜工作量。
listening.promptZh: badge of honour 在此描述甚麼？

options.en: The pride he attached to working alone, not proof that it improved the project.
options.zh: 他賦予獨做的自豪，不是改善項目的證明。

options.en: An official award given for completing every check accurately.
options.zh: 因每項核對準確而頒正式獎。

options.en: A decision to share the work before any checks were missed.
options.zh: 未漏核前已決定分工。

options.en: A report that he disliked having responsibility for the project.
options.zh: 報告他不喜歡負責項目。

listening.explanationZh: treated as說人物看法，but missed checks保留效果不支持自豪。

reply.promptZh: 他怎樣看待獨自做完整項目？
reply.promptEn: How did he view doing the whole project on his own?

options.en: He took pride in doing it all himself.
options.zh: 他以全自己做為榮。

options.en: He treated it as a badge of honour rather than a workload to share.
options.zh: 他把它當自豪標記，而非可分擔工作量。

options.en: He saw the solo effort as a sign of achievement.
options.zh: 他把獨做視作成就標記。

options.en: The amount he handled alone mattered to his sense of status.
options.zh: 他獨做的份量對其地位感有重要性。

reply.explanationZh: 四句描述他賦予的自豪，不等於確認做法好。

scene.promptZh: 人物把十年來每次都準時歸還外借道具當值得自豪的紀錄，沒有正式獎章。哪句準確？

options.en: She sees that reliable record as a badge of honour.
options.zh: 她把可靠紀錄視為自豪標記。

options.en: She received a physical medal from an official competition.
options.zh: 她從正式比賽得實體獎章。

options.en: She regards the record as something to hide rather than value.
options.zh: 她把紀錄當需隱藏而非重視的事。

scene.explanationZh: 角色重視紀錄可用比喻，未有實體獎或羞恥。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 a badge of honour 得出？

options.en: Someone regards a feature as a source of pride or status.
options.zh: 某人把特點視為自豪或地位來源。

options.en: The phrase itself confirms that the underlying action was wise and effective.
options.zh: 片語本身確認該行動明智有效。

options.en: Context may show approval or criticism of that pride.
options.zh: 情境可顯示認同或批評該自豪。

contrast.explanationZh: 報告自豪不自動認可行動。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說他以獨做為榮，所以就不用提漏核；你想如實評估。哪句最好？

options.en: We can describe his pride and still examine what the missed checks show.
options.zh: 可描述自豪，同時檢視漏核顯示甚麼。

options.en: Would highlighting his solo effort be enough for the review, without examining the missed checks?
options.zh: 評述只突出他獨做，不檢視漏核，是否已足夠？

options.en: Perhaps he felt embarrassed rather than proud about doing the project alone.
options.zh: 也許他對獨做項目感到尷尬，而非自豪。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已說他以獨做為榮，但漏核仍需評估；不能只讚份量，或把已表達的自豪改為尷尬。

speaking.en: He saw it as a badge of honour, but we still needed to consider the effect on the work.
speaking.zh: 他把它視為自豪標記，但我們仍需考慮對工作的影響。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清人物看法與效果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫人物小傳，一位退休館員把多年保留讀者手寫謝卡當作自己的自豪標記，並非要炫耀正式獎項。你想用這點介紹她重視與讀者的關係，不替所有館員下定義。用一至兩句英文描寫。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以館員重視的謝卡關係描寫自豪意義，保留個人視角及非正式獎，不把紀念物變客觀排名。

examples.en: She regarded the collection of readers’ thank-you cards as a badge of honour, a reminder of the relationships she valued. The cards mattered more to her than a formal award.
examples.zh: 她把讀者謝卡集視為自豪標記，提醒自己珍惜的關係。對她而言，卡比正式獎更重要。

examples.en: For this retired librarian, the handwritten cards were a badge of honour because they recalled years of helping readers find what they needed.
examples.zh: 對這位退休館員，手寫卡是自豪標記，因它們喚起多年幫讀者找所需的經歷。

takeaways.en: The old notebook became a badge of honour for the team that had built the project together.
takeaways.zh: 舊筆記本成為共同建立項目的團隊的自豪標記。

takeaways.en: He no longer treated working through every break as a badge of honour.
takeaways.zh: 他不再把每次小休都工作當自豪標記。

titleZh: 按慣常做法理所當然地做

brief.meaningEn: As a normal routine practice, without treating it as an unusual exception.
brief.meaningZh: 作為平常例行做法，不視為罕有例外。
brief.grammar: check/ask/record something as a matter of course; the phrase modifies how routinely the action is done.
brief.register: Established fairly formal phrase for ordinary practice. Distinct from as a matter of fact, which introduces a factual statement or correction.
brief.boundaryZh: 慣常做不保證每次無錯、已完成某次工作或沒有思考；需分清程序及實際紀錄。
brief.misconceptionZh: 平常會核對，不等於這份已核過；可以問該次是否有記錄。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明例行程序，保留當次完成狀態與查證。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The team checks the figures as a matter of course.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 22, table 1, row 10; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: We check the photograph credits as a matter of course before publication, but this issue’s final check is still on tomorrow’s list.
listening.zh: 刊登前，我們例行核照片署名，但本期最後核對仍在明天清單。
listening.promptZh: 慣常做法與本期進度怎樣？

options.en: Credit checking is routine, but this issue’s final check is still pending.
options.zh: 署名核對是慣常做法，但本期最後核對仍待做。

options.en: This issue’s final check has already been recorded as complete.
options.zh: 本期最後核對已記作完成。

options.en: Credits are checked only when a special complaint is made.
options.zh: 只有特別投訴才核署名。

options.en: This issue’s credit check is a new exception rather than part of the normal process.
options.zh: 本期署名核對是新例外，而非正常程序部分。

listening.explanationZh: 例行做法與tomorrow pending不同，不能報本次已完。

reply.promptZh: 刊登前，你們通常怎樣處理照片署名？
reply.promptEn: What do you usually do about photograph credits before publication?

options.en: We normally check the credits before publication.
options.zh: 我們刊前通常核署名。

options.en: We check them as a matter of course, though this issue’s final check is tomorrow.
options.zh: 我們例行核署名，但本期最後核對在明天。

options.en: The check is part of the regular publication process.
options.zh: 核對是平常刊登程序一部分。

options.en: We do not wait for a special complaint to include the credit check.
options.zh: 我們不等特別投訴才做署名核對。

reply.explanationZh: 四句答慣常做法，未把今期進度變完成。

scene.promptZh: 工作坊每次借工具後都按清單點算，不需等有人說遺失；今天仍未收尾。哪句準確？

options.en: We count the tools as a matter of course at the end of each workshop.
options.zh: 我們每次工作坊結束例行點工具。

options.en: Today’s count has already finished because a routine exists.
options.zh: 因有慣例，今天點算已完成。

options.en: The count happens only after a loss is reported.
options.zh: 只有報失後才點算。

scene.explanationZh: 正常收尾規則可描述，未收尾不能說已做。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 as a matter of course 得出？

options.en: The action is part of a normal routine.
options.zh: 行動是正常例行部分。

options.en: The particular instance has necessarily been completed correctly.
options.zh: 該次必定已正確完成。

options.en: The phrase concerns usual practice rather than an unusual exception.
options.zh: 說法關通常做法，而非罕有例外。

contrast.explanationZh: 有程序不確立當次紀錄與正確性。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「例行會查署名」，便問可否把本期標已核完；最後核對其實明天。哪句準確？

options.en: Keep it marked pending until tomorrow’s check is done, even though checking is our normal practice.
options.zh: 即使核對是平常做法，也先標待做，明天完成才改。

options.en: Yes, the routine is the completion record for this issue.
options.zh: 對，慣例就是本期完成紀錄。

options.en: Could we move this issue’s scheduled check into the optional tasks because checks are usually routine?
options.zh: 因核對通常屬例行，可否把本期原定核對移到選做任務？

dialogue.explanationZh: 例行核對仍要在本期實際執行；有慣例不能代替完成紀錄，也不使排定核對變選做。

speaking.en: We ask about permission as a matter of course, but I still need the answer for this particular photograph.
speaking.zh: 我們例行問許可，但這張照片的回覆仍需取得。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清慣例與當次資料。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你主持朋友的棋聚，每位新人來都會被問是否玩過，以便安排簡介。一位朋友以為你特別懷疑他的能力，你想有禮澄清這是對每人都問的慣常問題，並邀他告訴你想否先聽規則，不代他回答。用一至兩句英文回應。

examples.en: I ask everyone about their experience as a matter of course so I can offer the right introduction. Would you like a quick explanation of the rules before we begin?
examples.zh: 我例行問每人的經驗，以便提供合適簡介；開始前，你想先聽簡短規則說明嗎？

examples.en: We ask new players as a matter of course, not because we doubt your ability. Please tell me whether you would like an introduction or are ready to start.
examples.zh: 我們例行問新玩家，不是懷疑你能力；請告訴我想聽簡介，還是已可開始。

glossary.en: a quick explanation of the rules

writing.selfCheckZh: 解釋對每人問經驗的慣例及提供合適簡介的目的，直接邀對方說需要，不把提問當能力評定或代對方完成回答。

takeaways.en: The team records the source as a matter of course when adding a new quotation.
takeaways.zh: 小組加新引文時，例行記來源。

takeaways.en: We reviewed the route as a matter of course before giving the guide to first-time visitors.
takeaways.zh: 交指南給初訪者前，我們例行檢視路線。

brief.meaningEn: Rest or take a refreshing break so that energy or enthusiasm can return.
brief.meaningZh: 休息或作令人精神一振的轉換，恢復精力或熱情。
brief.grammar: recharge my/your/their batteries; recharged in past; possessive matches the person recovering energy.
brief.register: Established device metaphor for human energy. The person is not literally being charged electrically.
brief.boundaryZh: 可描述精神恢復，不保證問題全解、所有人同樣受用或特定生理效果；看個人體驗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 短暫轉換可有用，也可仍需處理工作，不能把恢復精神當任務已完成。
brief.outcomeZh: 能自然描述休息體驗，保留之後仍需做的事。

sources.sentence: Staff need time to recharge their batteries after a busy season.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 219, table 1, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: A quiet afternoon away from the event messages helped me recharge my batteries; when I returned, I had more energy to review the list, though the unfinished tasks were still there.
listening.zh: 暫離活動訊息的安靜下午幫我恢復精神；回來較有精力檢視清單，未完成工作仍在。
listening.promptZh: 下午休息帶來甚麼，而未帶來甚麼？

options.en: More energy for reviewing the list, not automatic completion of the tasks.
options.zh: 較多精力檢視清單，不是任務自動完成。

options.en: The speaker returned with the list already reviewed and no need for another look.
options.zh: 說話者回來時清單已檢視，毋須再看。

options.en: The speaker used the afternoon to plan replies to the event messages.
options.zh: 說話者用下午規劃活動訊息的回覆。

options.en: The improvement concerned how the list was organised rather than the speaker’s energy.
options.zh: 改善關乎清單的組織，而非說話者的精力。

listening.explanationZh: 休息後較有精力，才回來檢視清單；未完成工作仍在，不是已檢視、已規劃回覆或改清單組織。

reply.promptZh: 那個安靜下午對你有甚麼幫助？
reply.promptEn: How did the quiet afternoon help you?

options.en: I came back with more energy to review the task list.
options.zh: 我回來有更多精神檢視任務清單。

options.en: It helped me recharge my batteries before returning to the work.
options.zh: 回工作前，它幫我恢復精神。

options.en: The break refreshed me without removing the work that remained.
options.zh: 休息讓我精神一振，沒有除去剩餘工作。

options.en: I felt more ready to focus on the list afterwards.
options.zh: 之後我感到較能專注清單。

reply.explanationZh: 四句描述個人恢復，未把休息當代做工作。

scene.promptZh: 忙碌展期後，你暫停訊息一會、安靜讀喜歡的故事，之後較有精神整理紀錄。哪句貼切？

options.en: The quiet reading helped me recharge my batteries.
options.zh: 安靜閱讀幫我恢復精神。

options.en: Reading the story was part of sorting the exhibition records rather than a break from them.
options.zh: 讀故事是整理展覽紀錄一部分，而非暫離紀錄工作。

options.en: I felt ready to do the records because I had finished them before reading.
options.zh: 我覺得可處理紀錄，是因讀書前已把它們做完。

scene.explanationZh: 閱讀後較有精神整理紀錄，是個人恢復；不是閱讀本身屬紀錄工作，也未說已事先完成。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 recharged their batteries 得出？

options.en: They felt refreshed or recovered some energy.
options.zh: 他們精神一振或恢復一些精力。

options.en: Every problem waiting for them has been solved.
options.zh: 等他們處理的每個問題已解。

options.en: The context can explain what kind of break helped them.
options.zh: 情境可解釋甚麼休息有幫助。

contrast.explanationZh: 個人精神恢復不等於工作問題已解。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「你回來精神好了，那剩餘清單不用看了？」但還有未完成項目。哪句準確？

options.en: The break gives me more energy to review the remaining work; it does not replace that review.
options.zh: 休息給我更多精神檢視剩餘工作，不取代檢視。

options.en: Then I can leave the list unchecked and decide what remains from memory.
options.zh: 那我可不核清單，只靠記憶決定還剩甚麼。

options.en: Perhaps the quiet afternoon mainly reduced the number of tasks, rather than helping your energy.
options.zh: 也許安靜下午主要減少任務數量，而非改善精神。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已說休息改善精神、任務仍在，故應實際檢視清單，不以記憶代核對或誤說任務減少。

speaking.en: I needed time to recharge my batteries before I could give the next task proper attention.
speaking.zh: 我需時間恢復精神，才可好好專注下項任務。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再用人的精力理解比喻。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友替你安排旅行每段空檔都有活動，你想在兩天導覽之間留一個安靜下午休息，再好好參與翌日，不是拒絕整趟旅行。用一至兩句英文向朋友提出安排。
writing.selfCheckZh: 提出具體留白並說明想好好參與之後行程，不把休息變全拒旅行或保證所有人同感。

examples.en: Could we leave one quiet afternoon to recharge our batteries between the two guided days? I want to enjoy the next visit with more energy, not miss the whole trip.
examples.zh: 兩天導覽之間可留一個安靜下午恢復精神嗎？我想更有精神享受下次參觀，不是錯過整趟旅行。

examples.en: I would like some time to recharge my batteries rather than fill every gap with another activity. That would help me take part properly the following day.
examples.zh: 我想留時間恢復精神，不把每段空檔都塞另一活動。這會幫我翌日好好參與。

takeaways.en: They recharged their batteries during a quiet weekend before returning to the project.
takeaways.zh: 安靜周末期間，他們恢復精神，再回項目。

takeaways.en: I wanted to recharge my batteries, so I left a little space between the two busy days.
takeaways.zh: 我想恢復精神，所以在兩個忙日之間留點空間。

brief.meaningEn: Deal with urgent problems as they arise, often leaving less time for planned work.
brief.meaningZh: 逐一處理眼前突發急事，常令原定工作時間減少。
brief.grammar: spend the morning putting out fires; put out fires in past uses put; specify the problems in context.
brief.register: Established emergency-response metaphor in ordinary organisational work. Here no literal fire is implied.
brief.boundaryZh: 應急不一定沒用，也不表示已找根源或預防再發；需分清即時處理及長期整理。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可承認解急事的必要，同時安排檢視反覆原因，不把兩者互相排斥。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體描寫應急工作及尚未處理的根源問題。

sources.sentence: The director spent the morning putting out fires.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 23, table 1, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: I spent the morning putting out fires: a speaker’s file would not open, a room sign was missing and two bookings overlapped, so the planned review of our system had to wait.
listening.zh: 早上我不停應急：講者檔開不了、房牌不見、兩項預約重疊，原定系統檢視只好等。
listening.promptZh: putting out fires 描述甚麼？

options.en: Handling several immediate problems instead of the planned system review.
options.zh: 處理幾項即時問題，而非原定系統檢視。

options.en: Completing a preventive review before any event problem occurred.
options.zh: 活動出問題前已完成預防檢視。

options.en: The team’s time went into researching a new fire-safety programme for a future event.
options.zh: 團隊時間用於研究未來活動的新消防安全計劃。

options.en: The reported issues were set aside while the speaker completed the planned review.
options.zh: 說話者完成原定檢視時，把已報問題放到一旁。

listening.explanationZh: 檔案、房牌及預約是當下急事，原定系統檢視被延後；不是未來消防研究或先完成檢視。

reply.promptZh: 早上為甚麼沒做原定系統檢視？
reply.promptEn: Why did the planned system review not happen that morning?

options.en: The file, sign and overlapping bookings needed immediate attention.
options.zh: 檔、牌及預約重疊需立即處理。

options.en: I was putting out fires as several urgent problems arose.
options.zh: 幾項急事出現，我不停應急。

options.en: The immediate fixes used the time set aside for the review.
options.zh: 即時修補用了原定檢視時間。

options.en: We had to get the current activities working before returning to the wider process.
options.zh: 我們需先讓當前活動運作，再回較大程序。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給急事佔時理由，不把應急當已完成系統檢視。

scene.promptZh: 活動中你先補缺的桌牌、處理錯房號及臨時缺席，未能整理下次程序。哪句準確？

options.en: I was putting out fires rather than reviewing the process for next time.
options.zh: 我當時不停應急，不是在檢視下次程序。

options.en: The next event’s system review was completed before these issues arose.
options.zh: 這些問題出前，下次系統檢視已完成。

options.en: I set aside the reported problems so I could focus on the procedure for the next event.
options.zh: 我放下已報問題，專注下次活動程序。

scene.explanationZh: 當時先處理桌牌、房號及缺席等急事，尚未整理下次程序，不是先完成或優先做未來檢視。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 putting out fires 單獨得出？

options.en: Urgent problems are being dealt with in context.
options.zh: 情境中正處理急事。

options.en: Their underlying causes have all been removed for the future.
options.zh: 它們的根源已全部除去，往後不再有。

options.en: More detail can show whether planned work was delayed.
options.zh: 更多細節可顯示原定工作是否延後。

contrast.explanationZh: 即時處理與根源預防不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「房牌補好，是否預約系統也算改善了？」但你只處理當日急事。哪句最好？

options.en: The immediate fixes helped today; we still need to review why the booking clash happened.
options.zh: 即時修補幫了今天，仍需查預約衝突為何發生。

options.en: Yes, replacing the missing sign completes the booking-process review too.
options.zh: 對，補房牌也完成預約程序檢視。

options.en: We should focus the later review on buying spare signs rather than examining the booking clash.
options.zh: 之後檢視應集中買備用房牌，不查預約衝突。

dialogue.explanationZh: 補房牌解決一項即時需要，不代表已檢視預約程序；後續仍需查衝突，不只準備更多房牌。

speaking.en: We were putting out fires, so I want to make time later to look at the repeated causes.
speaking.zh: 我們當時不停應急，所以我想之後留時間看反覆原因。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清眼前修補及根源。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友以為你故意不回電話，其實下午你臨時替大樓處理住戶鎖門及入口故障，現在終於停下來。你想簡短解釋自己忙於應急、道歉，並約晚上八點再通話，不在這次訊息提出整套管理改革。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: I was putting out fires at the building all afternoon, arranging a locksmith and finding a temporary entrance for residents. I am sorry I missed your call; could we talk at eight?
examples.zh: 下午我在大樓不停應急，安排鎖匠及為住戶找臨時入口。抱歉沒接到電話；可否八點再談？

examples.en: I spent the afternoon putting out fires for the residents rather than ignoring you. Sorry about the missed call; I can give you my full attention at eight this evening.
examples.zh: 我下午忙於為住戶應急，不是在不理你。抱歉沒接電話；今晚八點我可好好專心跟你談。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以大樓急事解釋當時沒接電話，承認朋友受影響、道歉及另約八點，讓應急描述服務實際關係修補。

takeaways.en: The team spent the first hour putting out fires before it could return to the planned work.
takeaways.zh: 團隊先花一小時應急，再回原定工作。

takeaways.en: We put out fires during the event and saved the process review for the following morning.
takeaways.zh: 活動中我們應急，把程序檢視留翌晨。

brief.meaningEn: An activity or outlet that helps release accumulated tension.
brief.meaningZh: 幫助紓解累積緊張的活動或出口。
brief.grammar: act as/provide a pressure valve for someone; identify the outlet and the tension it helps relieve.
brief.register: A mechanical metaphor used for emotional or social pressure; the outlet does not necessarily remove the cause.
brief.boundaryZh: 紓壓不等於問題已解或適合所有人；不可由個人體驗保證健康效果。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可描述暫時放鬆，同時保留之後需處理的實際問題。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把出口的作用與問題的根源分清。

sources.sentence: Exercise acts as a pressure valve after work.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 23, table 1, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Our informal sketching hour acted as a pressure valve after the tense committee meeting: we could relax together, although the disagreement about the budget still needed a separate discussion.
listening.zh: 緊張委員會會議後，隨意畫畫的一小時成為紓壓出口：我們可一起放鬆，但預算分歧仍需另談。
listening.promptZh: 畫畫的作用及尚待處理的是甚麼？

options.en: It eased the tension without settling the budget disagreement.
options.zh: 它舒緩緊張，卻未解決預算分歧。

options.en: It was the meeting at which the budget was finally agreed.
options.zh: 那是終於議定預算的會議。

options.en: It gave the committee a new method for calculating the budget.
options.zh: 它給委員會新的預算計算方法。

options.en: It postponed a relaxed activity until after the disagreement had ended.
options.zh: 它把輕鬆活動延至分歧結束後。

listening.explanationZh: 先有緊張，再一起放鬆；預算仍需另談，不是已決或計算方法。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼那一小時對你們有幫助？
reply.promptEn: Why did the sketching hour help the committee?

options.en: It gave us a chance to relax after the tense discussion.
options.zh: 緊張討論後，它讓我們有機會放鬆。

options.en: It acted as a pressure valve while the budget issue remained unresolved.
options.zh: 預算仍未解決時，它成為紓壓出口。

options.en: We could release some tension by doing something informal together.
options.zh: 一起做隨意的活動，讓我們紓解一些緊張。

options.en: The shared break helped us feel less tense before returning to the disagreement.
options.zh: 再談分歧前，共同休息讓我們較不緊繃。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述舒緩，不聲稱預算已定。

scene.promptZh: 排練爭論後，幾位同學約定放下評分，輕鬆唱熟悉的歌，心情放鬆，但分工仍待重談。哪句準確？

options.en: The familiar songs provided a pressure valve without settling the division of work.
options.zh: 熟悉歌曲提供紓壓出口，卻未解決分工。

options.en: The relaxed singing was their final agreement on who would do each task.
options.zh: 輕鬆唱歌就是每人任務的最後協議。

options.en: They sang only after the disagreement and tension had both been resolved.
options.zh: 分歧和緊張都解決後，他們才唱歌。

scene.explanationZh: 歌唱舒緩情緒，分工仍未定；不要把作用或時間次序混淆。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a pressure valve 單獨推斷？

options.en: Something offers an outlet for tension.
options.zh: 某事提供紓解緊張的出口。

options.en: The cause of the tension has been resolved.
options.zh: 緊張的起因已解決。

options.en: Context can show what pressure is involved.
options.zh: 情境可交代涉及甚麼壓力。

contrast.explanationZh: 出口可有幫助，仍需另處理根源。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「既然畫畫後輕鬆了，就不用再談預算？」分歧仍在。哪句最好？

options.en: The break eased the mood; we still need to agree on the budget.
options.zh: 休息舒緩氣氛；我們仍需議定預算。

options.en: Could we take the improved mood as agreement with the budget proposal?
options.zh: 可否把氣氛改善當作同意預算方案？

options.en: Should we leave the budget discussion unscheduled and see whether the relaxed mood lasts?
options.zh: 應否不排預算討論，先看輕鬆氣氛能否維持？

dialogue.explanationZh: 情緒改善不是同意方案，也不能代替安排尚待處理的討論。

speaking.en: The informal session was a pressure valve, but it did not settle the question we still had to discuss.
speaking.zh: 隨意的聚會是紓壓出口，卻沒解決仍需討論的問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清紓壓與解決問題。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替長時間閉門製作模型的社團擬下月時間表，成員希望每周有一段不評作品、不談進度的散步時間；你想建議把它作為紓壓出口，但另排實際進度檢視。用一至兩句英文提案。
writing.selfCheckZh: 提出不評作品的散步時間及分開的進度檢視，讓紓壓出口與實際管理各有位置，不聲稱散步可自動解決進度。

examples.en: A weekly walk could be a pressure valve for the model-making group if we leave project reviews out of it. We can schedule a separate check on progress.
examples.zh: 若散步不評項目，每周散步可成模型製作小組的紓壓出口。我們可另排進度核對。

examples.en: Let us keep one unhurried walk as a pressure valve rather than turn it into another progress meeting. The practical review can have its own time.
examples.zh: 保留一次不趕急的散步作紓壓出口，不把它變另一次進度會議；實際檢視可另有時間。

takeaways.en: The evening games became a pressure valve during a demanding week of rehearsals.
takeaways.zh: 繁忙排練的一周，晚間遊戲成了紓壓出口。

takeaways.en: We wanted a pressure valve, not another session in which every idea would be assessed.
takeaways.zh: 我們想有紓壓出口，不是另一次每個想法都會被評核的活動。

brief.meaningEn: Direct attention away from work for a while.
brief.meaningZh: 讓注意力暫時離開工作。
brief.grammar: something takes my mind off work; I do something to take my mind off work; took/taken in past forms.
brief.register: Established mental-attention phrase. It describes a temporary change of focus, not forgetting how to do a job or resigning.
brief.boundaryZh: 暫時不想工作，不代表工作不重要、已完成或辭職；要看時間及注意力。
brief.misconceptionZh: 活動可轉移思緒，但返回時仍可能需處理工作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能交代暫時轉換注意力的體驗，保留之後安排。

sources.sentence: A weekend hike can take their mind off work.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 23, table 1, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Learning the steps for the community dance took my mind off work for an hour; I was concentrating on the music rather than replaying the difficult conversation with my manager.
listening.zh: 學社區舞蹈步法，讓我一小時暫時不想工作；我專注音樂，不再反覆想與主管的艱難對話。
listening.promptZh: 那一小時，說話者的注意力有何變化？

options.en: It moved from the work conversation to the dance and music.
options.zh: 它從工作對話轉到舞蹈及音樂。

options.en: The speaker used the dance hour to prepare a reply to the manager.
options.zh: 說話者用舞蹈時間準備回覆主管。

options.en: The speaker had already resolved the disagreement with the manager.
options.zh: 說話者已與主管解決分歧。

options.en: The speaker decided to leave the job before learning the dance.
options.zh: 學舞前，說話者決定離職。

listening.explanationZh: concentrating on music而非replaying conversation，是注意力轉換，不是對話已解或辭職。

reply.promptZh: 學舞那一小時為甚麼有幫助？
reply.promptEn: Why did learning the dance help you that evening?

options.en: I focused on the music instead of replaying the work conversation.
options.zh: 我專注音樂，不再反覆想工作對話。

options.en: The steps took my mind off work for a while.
options.zh: 步法讓我暫時不想工作。

options.en: Following the dance gave my attention something different to do.
options.zh: 跟着跳舞讓我專注另一件事。

options.en: For that hour, I was thinking about movement rather than my manager’s words.
options.zh: 那一小時，我想動作而非主管說的話。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答暫時轉移注意力，不把它改為工作已解。

scene.promptZh: 你做陶泥杯時一直專注形狀，暫時沒想今天的電郵，晚點仍打算回覆。哪句貼切？

options.en: Working with the clay took my mind off work for a while.
options.zh: 弄陶泥讓我暫時不想工作。

options.en: I used the pottery session to organise my replies to the work emails.
options.zh: 我用陶藝時間整理工作電郵回覆。

options.en: I finished the email replies before I began shaping the cup.
options.zh: 塑杯前，我已回完電郵。

scene.explanationZh: 專注杯形是轉移，未提整理或先回完電郵。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像 take your mind off work 的本課意思？

options.en: Temporarily concentrating on something outside work.
options.zh: 暫時專注工作以外事情。

options.en: Continuing to rehearse the work discussion throughout the break.
options.zh: 休息期間繼續反覆想工作討論。

options.en: An activity helping someone stop dwelling on work for a while.
options.zh: 活動幫人暫時不再掛念工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 若一直想工作，注意力並未移開。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「既然跳舞時沒想工作，那與主管的事已解決？」你尚未再談。哪句最好？

options.en: It gave me a break from thinking about it; the conversation still needs a follow-up.
options.zh: 它讓我暫時不想那件事；對話仍需跟進。

options.en: Could I treat that hour away from the issue as the end of the disagreement?
options.zh: 可否把那一小時沒想問題，當作分歧已結束？

options.en: Should I use the next dance session to plan every point for the manager?
options.zh: 我應否用下次舞蹈時間規劃跟主管談的每一點？

dialogue.explanationZh: 轉移注意力不解決分歧；若全程規劃工作，便失去這種轉換。

speaking.en: The activity took my mind off work for a while, though I still needed to follow up the next day.
speaking.zh: 活動讓我暫時不想工作，但翌日仍需跟進。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說暫時轉換注意力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在旅行途中每次休息都讀工作訊息，朋友提議一起按紙本地圖找老街建築細節。你想接受，並約定晚間才集中查一次訊息，不是表示不再負責工作。用一至兩句英文回應朋友。
writing.selfCheckZh: 接受朋友共同觀察的具體活動，交代晚間再查訊息，保留暫時注意力轉換與責任安排。

examples.en: Looking for the details on the old buildings could take my mind off work this afternoon. I will check the messages once tonight instead of reading them at every stop.
examples.zh: 下午找老建築細節，可讓我暫時不想工作。我會今晚集中查一次訊息，不每站都看。

examples.en: Let us follow the paper map and notice the buildings together; that should help take my mind off work for a while. I can return to the messages this evening.
examples.zh: 一起按紙本地圖留意建築吧；這應可幫我暫時不想工作。今晚我可再看訊息。

takeaways.en: The puzzle took her mind off work during the journey home.
takeaways.zh: 回家路上，拼圖讓她暫時不想工作。

takeaways.en: I wanted something that would take my mind off work, so I joined the evening choir.
takeaways.zh: 我想做些能暫時轉移工作思緒的事，所以參加晚間合唱團。

brief.meaningEn: Relax and enjoy yourself with less formality or restraint.
brief.meaningZh: 放鬆享受，不再那麼拘謹或正式。
brief.grammar: let your/their hair down; let is also the past form; possessive matches the person relaxing.
brief.register: Informal established idiom, not a literal instruction about hairstyle. It need not imply losing control or ignoring others.
brief.boundaryZh: 放鬆不代表不顧界線、強迫別人同樣參與或一定飲酒；可按個人方式享受。
brief.misconceptionZh: 重點是從正式拘謹轉為自在，不由外表髮型推斷心情。
brief.outcomeZh: 能自然描寫放鬆氣氛，保留他人的選擇。

listening.en: After the formal presentations, the organisers let their hair down over a friendly quiz, laughing at their own guesses rather than keeping their polished stage manner.
listening.zh: 正式簡報後，主辦者玩友善問答放鬆，笑自己的猜測，不再維持台上那種精緻正式的表現。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼改變支持 let their hair down？

options.en: Their manner became relaxed and playful after the formal work.
options.zh: 正式工作後，他們變得自在、愛玩。

options.en: They continued the formal presentations in exactly the same manner.
options.zh: 他們以完全相同方式繼續正式簡報。

options.en: They organised the quiz as another assessed presentation.
options.zh: 他們把問答辦成另一次評分簡報。

options.en: They gave the quiz to a different team and stayed on stage.
options.zh: 他們把問答交另一組，自己留台上。

listening.explanationZh: laughing at guesses及不再維持台上表現，說明由正式轉自在。

reply.promptZh: 簡報後，主辦者怎樣放鬆？
reply.promptEn: How did the organisers relax after the presentations?

options.en: They laughed together over a friendly quiz.
options.zh: 他們一起玩友善問答、歡笑。

options.en: They let their hair down instead of keeping their stage manner.
options.zh: 他們不再維持台上表現，放鬆享受。

options.en: They became less formal and enjoyed guessing the answers.
options.zh: 他們不再那麼正式，享受猜答案。

options.en: The quiz gave them a playful change after the presentations.
options.zh: 簡報後，問答讓他們輕鬆轉換一下。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均描寫較自在的參與方式。

scene.promptZh: 頒獎儀式後，平日說話很正式的同事也加入輕鬆唱歌，自己挑一首喜歡的歌。哪句貼切？

options.en: She let her hair down and joined the informal singing.
options.zh: 她放鬆一下，加入輕鬆唱歌。

options.en: She treated the singing as another formal acceptance speech.
options.zh: 她把唱歌當另一次正式致謝演說。

options.en: She stayed apart because she wanted to preserve the ceremony’s formal manner.
options.zh: 她為維持儀式的正式方式而不加入。

scene.explanationZh: 加入輕鬆唱歌是自在轉換，不是正式致謝或保持距離。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 let their hair down 單獨得出？

options.en: They relaxed and behaved less formally.
options.zh: 他們放鬆、不再那麼正式。

options.en: They pressured other people to join every activity.
options.zh: 他們強迫其他人參加每項活動。

options.en: Context can show how they enjoyed themselves.
options.zh: 情境可顯示他們怎樣享受。

contrast.explanationZh: 自己的放鬆不表示要別人放棄選擇。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想叫安靜坐着的人也一定上台唱，說這才算放鬆；對方只想聽。哪句最好？

options.en: Let people relax in their own way; listening can be part of enjoying the evening too.
options.zh: 讓大家按自己的方式放鬆；聽歌也可以是享受晚會。

options.en: Could we put their name on the singing list before asking, to help them relax?
options.zh: 為幫他們放鬆，可否先不問就填他們上唱歌名單？

options.en: Should we end the singing because someone prefers to listen?
options.zh: 有人較想聽，我們應否就結束唱歌？

dialogue.explanationZh: 可保留唱歌及聽歌的選擇，不預代同意，也不因參與方式不同全停。

speaking.en: We could let our hair down without expecting everyone to enjoy the evening in the same way.
speaking.zh: 我們可自在放鬆，不必期待每人以相同方式享受晚會。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說較自在的相處。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：新團員以為每次聚會都像考核，遲遲不敢提出趣味點子；你邀請他參加周五不評分的故事遊戲，可自願接一句，也可先聽，想讓他知道可以自在一些。用一至兩句英文邀請。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用不評分故事遊戲邀請自在參與，保留先聽或接一句的選擇，不用強迫上台證明放鬆。

examples.en: Come to Friday’s story game and let your hair down; it is not another assessment. You can add a line when you feel ready or just listen at first.
examples.zh: 周五來故事遊戲放鬆吧；不是另一次考核。你準備好可接一句，或先聽。

examples.en: The game is a chance for us to let our hair down and try playful ideas without being marked. There is no need to perform a polished speech.
examples.zh: 遊戲讓我們放鬆，試趣味點子而不被評分，不需表演精緻演說。

takeaways.en: After the exhibition closed, the volunteers let their hair down over a relaxed meal.
takeaways.zh: 展覽結束後，義工在輕鬆飯聚自在放鬆。

takeaways.en: She felt able to let her hair down once the conversation stopped being an interview.
takeaways.zh: 談話不再像訪問後，她覺得可自在放鬆。

brief.meaningEn: Extremely difficult to obtain and therefore highly valued.
brief.meaningZh: 極難得到，因而十分珍貴。
brief.grammar: like gold dust / be gold dust; both describe something scarce and therefore especially valuable. This is figurative, not literal gold powder.
brief.register: Established figurative expression, especially in British English. Like gold dust is a comparison; be gold dust is a direct metaphor. Neither requires a high sale price or literal gold.
brief.boundaryZh: 需有稀少難得及珍惜的情境，不只泛指好；未必花錢買或物品實含黃金。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一段時間、機會或實物都可珍貴，但不能只由昂貴便推數量稀少。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用比喻描述難得的資源並說明其稀缺。

listening.en: A free practice room was like gold dust during festival week: most rooms were booked from morning to night, so we valued the short slot the caretaker found for us.
listening.zh: 節慶周空練習室十分難得：大部分房早到晚已訂滿，所以管理員找到的短時段讓我們很珍惜。
listening.promptZh: 這個比喻有甚麼具體依據？

options.en: Available rooms were scarce, making the short slot valuable to the group.
options.zh: 可用房稀少，令短時段對小組珍貴。

options.en: The room had the highest hire price in the building.
options.zh: 那房在大樓租價最高。

options.en: The group had booked the same room for every day of the festival.
options.zh: 小組已訂節慶每天同一房。

options.en: The room was valued mainly for its expensive interior decoration.
options.zh: 房間主要因昂貴室內裝飾而被珍惜。

listening.explanationZh: 大部分已訂，短空檔難得；沒有價格或裝飾依據。

reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼珍惜那短短的房間時段？
reply.promptEn: Why did you value that short room booking?

options.en: Almost all the rooms were already booked.
options.zh: 幾乎所有房都已訂滿。

options.en: A free room was like gold dust during that week.
options.zh: 那周空房十分難得珍貴。

options.en: We had very few opportunities to practise in an available room.
options.zh: 我們很少有機會在空房練習。

options.en: The caretaker found a rare opening when we needed rehearsal space.
options.zh: 我們需排練地方時，管理員找到罕有空檔。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給稀少而珍惜的理由。

scene.promptZh: 某社區舊報刊僅剩幾份完整號數，你想查一段歷史，找到一份可讀原本便十分珍惜，不知道其市場價。哪句貼切？

options.en: A readable original is like gold dust for this research.
options.zh: 對這研究，可讀原本稀少珍貴。

options.en: The copy’s market price is already confirmed to be very high.
options.zh: 這份的市場價已確認很高。

options.en: Complete copies are easy to replace from a large available stock.
options.zh: 可從大量現貨輕易補完整本。

scene.explanationZh: 僅少量完整本支持難得，不是已知市場價或易補存貨。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 like gold dust？

options.en: A needed resource is very scarce and therefore prized.
options.zh: 所需資源很稀少，因而被珍惜。

options.en: An ordinary item is readily available, and only its appearance is being praised.
options.zh: 普通物品隨處可得，只因外觀受讚。

options.en: A rare opening is especially valuable when most options are unavailable.
options.zh: 大多選項不可用時，罕有空檔特別珍貴。

contrast.explanationZh: 外觀好但隨處可得，未給稀缺基礎。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴把「房間難得」改成「全樓最昂貴」，但你只知道已訂滿。哪句最好？

options.en: That booking was like gold dust because rooms were scarce; we have not compared hire prices.
options.zh: 房間難訂，這次預約極其珍貴；但我們未比較租價。

options.en: The shortage of rooms establishes that this room has the highest hire price.
options.zh: 房間短缺確立了這間房的租價最高。

options.en: Could we describe the decoration instead and leave out why the slot mattered?
options.zh: 可否改寫裝飾，省去這時段為何重要？

dialogue.explanationZh: 珍貴來自難訂，不能以供應直接定價，也不需轉到未給的裝飾。

speaking.en: A spare hour was like gold dust that week, so I used it for the task that needed quiet concentration.
speaking.zh: 那周空閒一小時十分難得，所以我用它做需安靜專注的工作。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說難得與珍惜的關係。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為老店口述歷史招募仍記得最早店面的人，已聯絡多處，只有一位願意講且下周有半小時。你想請團隊先確認問題及錄音準備，好好用這難得機會，不替受訪者的記憶保證全對。用一至兩句英文提醒。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出經多次查詢僅得一個短訪問機會，提出事前準備及事後核實；珍貴不等於每項記憶必準。

examples.en: Time with someone who remembers the first shop is like gold dust for this project. Let us prepare the questions before next week’s half-hour interview.
examples.zh: 對這項目，能與記得首間店的人談話的時間十分難得。下周半小時訪問前，我們先備問題。

examples.en: This interview opportunity is like gold dust after so many enquiries. We should check the recording equipment beforehand and still verify the details afterwards.
examples.zh: 問過那麼多地方後，這訪問機會十分難得。我們應事前查錄音設備，事後仍核實細節。

takeaways.en: A few quiet minutes were like gold dust while the house was being repaired.
takeaways.zh: 房子維修期間，幾分鐘安靜時間十分難得珍貴。

takeaways.en: In the crowded clinic, an uninterrupted ten minutes was gold dust for the duty nurse.
takeaways.zh: 在繁忙的診所，連續不受打擾的十分鐘對當值護士極其珍貴。

brief.meaningEn: Have a very good effect or produce marked improvement.
brief.meaningZh: 產生很好的效果或明顯改善。
brief.grammar: work/do wonders for something; worked/did/has done wonders; work and do are established variants of this idiom.
brief.register: Informal emphatic praise, often somewhat exaggerated. A specific observed benefit is preferable to an unsupported universal promise.
brief.boundaryZh: 說效果很好，不保證所有問題已解、對所有人有效或有精確量化改善；本課用日常可觀察效果。
brief.misconceptionZh: 明顯改善某部分，不等於全部完成，也不能代替未做的測試。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體讚賞改動的作用，交代仍待檢查的部分。

listening.en: Putting the tool names beside their storage hooks worked wonders for the workshop handover: newcomers found the right place much faster, though we still had to check the borrowing records.
listening.zh: 把工具名放在存放掛鈎旁，讓工作坊交接明顯改善：新人快得多找到位置，但仍需核借用紀錄。
listening.promptZh: 改善的是甚麼，尚未取代甚麼？

options.en: Finding storage places became quicker; record checking remained necessary.
options.zh: 找存放位置更快，核紀錄仍有需要。

options.en: The tool labels replaced the need to keep borrowing records.
options.zh: 工具標籤取代保留借用紀錄的需要。

options.en: The team confirmed that every newcomer already knew the storage system before the labels.
options.zh: 小組確認加標前每位新人已熟悉存放系統。

options.en: The change mainly improved how attractive the borrowing forms looked.
options.zh: 改動主要改善借用表外觀。

listening.explanationZh: 明說找到位置更快，不是免核紀錄、原已熟悉或表格外觀。

reply.promptZh: 工具名放掛鈎旁有甚麼幫助？
reply.promptEn: How did putting the tool names beside the hooks help?

options.en: Newcomers could find the correct storage place much faster.
options.zh: 新人可快得多找到正確存放位置。

options.en: It worked wonders for finding the right hook during handover.
options.zh: 交接時，它讓找正確掛鈎的情況明顯改善。

options.en: The names made the storage arrangement much easier to follow.
options.zh: 名稱讓存放安排容易明白得多。

options.en: People spent less time working out where a tool belonged.
options.zh: 大家花較少時間弄清工具放哪。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答已觀察的位置辨識改善。

scene.promptZh: 你把長篇交通指引分成出閘、轉彎、入門三段，再加地標；試走者少問路，但仍需確認新開側門的時間。哪句準確？

options.en: The clearer directions worked wonders, though the side entrance times still need checking.
options.zh: 清楚指引帶來很好的改善，側門時間仍需查。

options.en: The trial showed the original long paragraph was easier to follow.
options.zh: 試走顯示原本長段落較易跟。

options.en: The revised directions confirmed the side entrance hours without another check.
options.zh: 新指引毋須再查，就確認側門開放時間。

scene.explanationZh: 少問路支持明顯改善，未核時間仍需另查。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 worked wonders 單獨得出？

options.en: The speaker judges the effect very positively.
options.zh: 說話者對效果評價很正面。

options.en: All remaining checks can be omitted because success is guaranteed.
options.zh: 因保證成功，可省去所有剩餘核對。

options.en: Context can identify which improvement was observed.
options.zh: 情境可指出觀察到哪項改善。

contrast.explanationZh: 強烈稱讚不是免除核對或保證全部成功。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「標籤效果好，就不用核誰借了工具？」但標籤只處理位置。哪句最好？

options.en: The labels help with location; we still need the records to know who borrowed each tool.
options.zh: 標籤幫找位置；要知誰借工具，仍需紀錄。

options.en: Could we use the labelled hooks as our complete list of current borrowers?
options.zh: 可否用有名掛鈎作目前借用者的完整名單？

options.en: Should we postpone the borrower check until someone reports a missing tool?
options.zh: 應否等有人報工具不見，才核借用者？

dialogue.explanationZh: 位置提示與借用狀態不同；不能用標籤代名單或只待報失。

speaking.en: The small change worked wonders for the handover, but we still checked the details it did not cover.
speaking.zh: 小改動讓交接明顯改善，但我們仍核它未涵蓋的細節。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再具體說改善的範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為外婆整理多年未標註的家族照片，改成每次只看五張、即時記她說的名字，談話順暢得多；但有些年份她不確定。你想向家人交代這方法的好處，並把未確定年份留待另查。用一至兩句英文報告。
writing.selfCheckZh: 具體交代分小組觀看讓談話及記名改善，保留年份不確定；不把效果好變所有記憶已證實。

examples.en: Looking at five photographs at a time worked wonders for our conversation, and we could record the names as Grandma recalled them. We will check the uncertain years separately.
examples.zh: 每次看五張照片，讓談話明顯改善，我們可在外婆想起時即時記名字。不確定年份會另查。

examples.en: The smaller groups of photographs have done wonders for keeping the conversation clear. That does not settle every date, so I have marked the uncertain years for checking.

brief.meaningEn: Set a boundary that keeps two areas of life or activity from intruding on one another.
brief.meaningZh: 訂明界線，避免生活或活動的兩個範圍互相侵佔。
brief.grammar: Draw a line between two named areas of life or draw a line around my/your/his/her/our/their time to set a practical limit on availability; drew/has drawn. In the around form, say what time is protected and from which demand.
brief.register: Established boundary metaphor. Around their time is a source-attested extension for protecting availability; it is not a literal line around a clock or a claim that all contact must stop.
brief.boundaryZh: between 可分清兩項活動的界線；around their time 強調保護可用時間。兩者都需交代具體安排，也可保留真正急事的聯絡途徑，不表示完全切斷聯繫。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可明定回訊息時段及真正急事的處理，不必把界線說成所有聯絡都禁止。
brief.outcomeZh: 能清楚提出具體界線及必要安排。

listening.en: I drew a line between work and family time by leaving routine messages until the next morning, while giving the duty colleague a separate number for urgent problems.
listening.zh: 我把例行訊息留翌晨，為工作與家庭時間訂明界線；同時給當值同事另一號碼處理急事。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣實際訂界線？

options.en: Routine messages wait; urgent problems have a separate contact route.
options.zh: 例行訊息等候，急事另有聯絡途徑。

options.en: All work contact is refused regardless of urgency.
options.zh: 不論急不急，所有工作聯絡都拒絕。

options.en: Family time is used to clear routine messages before urgent calls.
options.zh: 家庭時間先清例行訊息，再接急事電話。

options.en: The colleague takes over all of the speaker’s work permanently.
options.zh: 同事永久接手說話者全部工作。

listening.explanationZh: 例行留翌晨，急事有另一號碼，界線具體而非完全斷聯。

reply.promptZh: 你怎樣避免例行工作佔去家庭時間？
reply.promptEn: How do you stop routine work from taking over family time?

options.en: I leave routine messages until morning and provide a separate route for urgent matters.
options.zh: 例行訊息留早上，急事另有途徑。

options.en: I draw a line between work and family time by separating routine replies from urgent contact.
options.zh: 我把例行回覆與急事聯絡分開，為工作與家庭時間訂界線。

options.en: I do not clear the ordinary message queue during family time.
options.zh: 家庭時間不清一般訊息隊列。

options.en: The duty colleague knows how to reach me for urgent issues without using the routine message stream.
options.zh: 當值同事知道怎樣為急事聯絡我，不用例行訊息串。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代具體時間及聯絡安排。

scene.promptZh: 你答應課後教社團一小時，結束後需照顧家人，將額外個別問題改約下次，不是拒絕再教。哪句貼切？

options.en: I need to draw a line around my time for the club: the agreed teaching hour ends before my family commitments.
options.zh: 我需要為給社團的時間訂界線：按約定教一小時後，我要履行家庭責任。

options.en: I am ending all involvement with the club after this lesson.
options.zh: 這課後我會結束與社團所有關係。

options.en: The agreed hour includes individual questions for the rest of the evening.
options.zh: 約定一小時包括餘下整晚個別問題。

scene.explanationZh: 已約定一小時，之後另約額外問題，正是為社團所佔用的時間訂界線；不是完全退出或無限延伸。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以展現本課 draw a line between 的實際界線？

options.en: Agreeing when routine requests will receive replies.
options.zh: 議定甚麼時候回覆例行請求。

options.en: Saying two activities have different names without setting any limit on their overlap.
options.zh: 只說兩活動名稱不同，沒訂交疊的限制。

options.en: Separating scheduled support from additional appointments.
options.zh: 分開原定支援與額外預約。

contrast.explanationZh: 本課需實際範圍或安排，不只命名分類。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「有界線就連急事都不能聯絡你」，但你已留急事號碼。哪句最好？

options.en: We can draw a line between routine messages and urgent contact: urgent calls have a separate number.
options.zh: 我們可為例行訊息與緊急聯絡訂界線：急事另有專用號碼。

options.en: The separate number means routine replies should also continue throughout family time.
options.zh: 另有號碼，表示家庭時間也應繼續例行回覆。

options.en: The urgent number replaces the need to agree on when ordinary messages are answered.
options.zh: 急事號碼可取代議定一般訊息回覆時段。

dialogue.explanationZh: 例行訊息與急事有不同安排；為兩者訂界線不等於急事不能聯絡，也不延伸成例行無時限回覆。

speaking.en: I want to draw a line between agreed support time and extra requests, while keeping a clear route for urgent issues.
speaking.zh: 我想在約定支援時間與額外請求間訂界線，同時保留清楚急事途徑。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說具體界線。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與朋友合租製作室，一人想把共同桌面當私人長期存放區，令你無法工作；你想議定共同桌面每日收清、私人未完作品放各自架，不是結束合作。用一至兩句英文提出安排。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以每日收清桌面、個人物品放架提出可執行界線，保留合作與共同使用，不只泛說私人物品不同。

examples.en: We should draw a line between shared working space and personal storage: let us clear the main table each day and keep unfinished pieces on our own shelves. That would let us both keep working here.
examples.zh: 我們應為共同工作空間與私人存放訂界線：每天收清大桌，未完成作品放各自架，讓彼此都可繼續在這裏工作。

examples.en: I want to draw a line between using the shared table and leaving work there overnight. Could we agree to use our separate shelves for unfinished pieces?
examples.zh: 我想在使用共同桌面與把作品留過夜間訂界線；可否議定未完作品放各自架？

takeaways.en: She drew a line between the agreed rehearsal time and extra coaching that needed another appointment.
takeaways.zh: 她在約定排練時間與需另約的額外指導間訂界線。

takeaways.en: We need to draw a line between shared supplies and items people have brought for their own projects.
takeaways.zh: 我們需在共用材料與各人為私人項目帶來的物品間訂界線。

titleZh: 把事情建立在不穩基礎上

target.pattern: (?:\bbuild(?:ing|s)? a house on sand\b|\bbuilt a house on sand\b)|(?:\b(?:build|builds|built|building) on sand\b)

brief.meaningEn: Developing a plan or undertaking on an unreliable foundation.
brief.meaningZh: 把計劃或事情建立在不可靠的基礎上。
brief.grammar: build a house on sand / build on sand; both mean base a plan on unreliable assumptions. Build, builds, built and building are usable forms.
brief.register: Conventional building image, often in an explicit comparison. It criticises the foundation, not necessarily the intentions or effort.
brief.boundaryZh: 需指出不可靠的資料、假設或安排；不是凡新計劃都必失敗，也不表示已實際倒塌。
brief.misconceptionZh: 投入更多修飾未必補到基礎，應先查關鍵假設。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明基礎弱在哪裏及提出可驗證的下一步。

sources.sentence: Planning around uncertain dates can feel like building on sand.

listening.en: Planning a month of sessions around an unconfirmed room booking would be like building a house on sand, so we checked the venue before inviting the speakers.
listening.zh: 圍繞未確認房間預約排一個月活動，就像把屋建在沙上，所以邀講者前我們先查場地。
listening.promptZh: 不穩基礎及下一步是甚麼？

options.en: The room was unconfirmed, so the venue was checked before invitations.
options.zh: 房間未確認，所以邀請前先查場地。

options.en: The speakers had already declined because they disliked the programme.
options.zh: 講者因不喜歡節目已拒絕。

options.en: A confirmed room booking was abandoned to change the decoration.
options.zh: 為改裝飾而放棄已確認預約。

options.en: The month of sessions had already failed before any checks.
options.zh: 未核對前，一個月活動已失敗。

listening.explanationZh: 關鍵是未確認場地；比喻警告基礎風險，不是已失敗或講者動機。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼先查場地才邀講者？
reply.promptEn: Why did you check the venue before inviting the speakers?

options.en: The session plan depended on a room we had not confirmed.
options.zh: 活動計劃依賴尚未確認的房間。

options.en: Planning around that uncertainty would be like building a house on sand.
options.zh: 圍繞那不確定安排，就像把屋建在沙上。

options.en: We needed a reliable location before making the rest of the arrangements.
options.zh: 作其餘安排前，我們需可靠場地。

options.en: The invitations would rest on an assumption unless we checked the booking.
options.zh: 若不核預約，邀請便建立在假設上。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出場地是後續安排基礎。

scene.promptZh: 你想根據一份沒有日期、未知仍否有效的價目表設計活動套餐，還沒詢問店方。哪句警告貼切？

options.en: Using that unchecked price list would be like building a house on sand.
options.zh: 使用未核的價目表，就像把屋建在沙上。

options.en: The old list confirms what the shop will charge for the next event.
options.zh: 舊表確認店方下次活動會收甚麼價。

options.en: The undated list already confirms that the shop can supply the proposed group size.
options.zh: 沒有日期的價目表已確認店方能供應提議的人數。

scene.explanationZh: 未核價目表的有效期及適用安排，不能把它當目前收費或供應人數已確認；先查支撐套餐的基本資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像 building a house on sand 的比喻？

options.en: A later plan depends on a critical assumption that has not been checked.
options.zh: 後續計劃依賴未核的關鍵假設。

options.en: A team develops a plan from verified essentials and revisits them when conditions change.
options.zh: 團隊從核實要點發展計劃，情況改變時再檢視。

options.en: Extra work is added before the necessary support is secured.
options.zh: 必要支援未確保前就加工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 基礎已核且持續檢視，不符合不可靠基礎。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想先做精緻邀請卡才查房間，說外觀好就較穩妥。哪句最好？

options.en: Designing the card before confirming the room would be building on sand; let us check the booking first.
options.zh: 未確認房間就先設計邀請卡，等於把計劃建立在不穩固的基礎上；先查清預約吧。

options.en: We should finish the card design and treat the venue line as settled for now.
options.zh: 先完成卡片設計，暫把場地一行當已定。

options.en: Let us choose a more impressive room description before checking whether it is available.
options.zh: 先選更吸引的房間描述，再查是否可用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 精緻表述不提供場地承諾，應先核支撐邀請的安排。

speaking.en: It would be like building a house on sand if we expanded the plan before checking its central assumption.
speaking.zh: 若未核核心假設就擴計劃，就像把屋建在沙上。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明不穩基礎。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替社區整理老照片人物故事，一位朋友只憑相似面貌就認定某人是知名店主，想寫出整段生平。你想先查相片來源、日期及在場者，不要把猜測寫成故事基礎。用一至兩句英文提出建議。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把未核身分明確作不穩基礎，提出查來源日期及在場者，不由相像直接斷言是或不是店主。

examples.en: Writing a whole biography from a resemblance would be like building a house on sand. Let us check the photograph’s source and date before deciding who the person is.
examples.zh: 只憑相像便寫整段生平，就像把屋建在沙上；決定那人身分前，先查相片來源及日期。

examples.en: We would be building a house on sand if we treated that guessed identity as the basis for the story. We should ask someone who was there and compare the available records first.
examples.zh: 若把猜測身分當故事基礎，就像把屋建在沙上；應先問在場者，並比較現有紀錄。

takeaways.en: Expanding the timetable without confirmed tutors would be like building a house on sand.
takeaways.zh: 未確認導師就擴時間表，就像把屋建在沙上。

takeaways.en: They were building on sand by budgeting from an unverified grant estimate.
takeaways.zh: 他們以未核實的資助估算編預算，等於把計劃建在不穩固的基礎上。

titleZh: 在已有基礎上進一步發展

brief.meaningEn: Use existing knowledge, achievement or resources as a basis for further development.
brief.meaningZh: 以已有知識、成果或資源為基礎進一步發展。
brief.grammar: build on earlier work/a skill/what we learned; built in past; distinguish the prior foundation from the added development.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb in learning and planning, figurative here. It does not mean copying everything unchanged or starting from nothing.
brief.boundaryZh: 需有承接的已有基礎及新進展；不保證舊方法每部分都適用。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以保留有用部分並調整其他部分，不是只重做同一件事或全盤丟棄。
brief.outcomeZh: 能清楚說明沿用甚麼及新增甚麼。

listening.en: The next workshop will build on the group’s measuring practice by asking them to make a simple folding stand; they will use the same measuring skill in a new task rather than repeat the worksheet.
listening.zh: 下次工作坊會承接小組量度練習，請他們做簡單摺架；在新任務用同樣量度技巧，而非重做工作紙。
listening.promptZh: 已有基礎與新發展是甚麼？

options.en: Measuring skills will be applied to making a folding stand.
options.zh: 量度技巧將用於製作摺架。

options.en: The measuring worksheet will be repeated without a new task.
options.zh: 只重做量度工作紙，沒有新任務。

options.en: The new task will begin without using the earlier measuring practice.
options.zh: 新任務不會使用先前量度練習。

options.en: The group has already finished making the stand during the earlier worksheet.
options.zh: 小組在早前工作紙期間已做好摺架。

listening.explanationZh: 已有量度技巧支援新製作，不是原樣重複、全棄或已完成。

reply.promptZh: 下次活動會怎樣使用之前的量度練習？
reply.promptEn: How will the next workshop use the earlier measuring practice?

options.en: The group will use those skills to make a folding stand.
options.zh: 小組將用那些技巧做摺架。

options.en: The workshop will build on the measuring practice through a new making task.
options.zh: 工作坊會透過新製作任務，承接量度練習。

options.en: The earlier practice provides a basis for applying measurement to a useful object.
options.zh: 早前練習為把量度用於實用物件提供基礎。

options.en: They will take what they learned about measuring into the next project.
options.zh: 他們將把量度所學帶入下一個項目。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出承接技巧及新用途。

scene.promptZh: 學生已學會描述照片，你下一課想請他們用兩張照片比較前後變化，而非再逐張列物件。哪句貼切？

options.en: We will build on their descriptions by comparing changes across two photographs.
options.zh: 我們將承接描述技巧，比較兩張照片的變化。

options.en: We will repeat the same object list without adding a comparison.
options.zh: 我們會重做同一物件清單，不加比較。

options.en: We will set aside everything they learned about describing photographs.
options.zh: 我們會放下他們所學的全部照片描述技巧。

scene.explanationZh: 比較承接描述並加新要求，不是原樣重複或完全放下。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像本課 build on？

options.en: Using a familiar technique for a more demanding task.
options.zh: 用熟悉技巧做要求較高任務。

options.en: Discarding the earlier work and beginning with no connection to it.
options.zh: 丟棄早前工作，重新開始且與它無關。

options.en: Extending a useful finding through a further investigation.
options.zh: 透過進一步研究延伸有用發現。

contrast.explanationZh: 完全斷開已有基礎，不是承接發展。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴以為承接量度練習就是原樣再派同一工作紙，你想加入摺架應用。哪句最好？

options.en: Keep the measuring skill as the foundation and apply it to the stand.
options.zh: 以量度技巧為基礎，應用到摺架。

options.en: Let us use the identical worksheet again and leave the stand out.
options.zh: 再用完全相同工作紙，省去摺架吧。

options.en: We should avoid the old measuring method so the stand task feels entirely new.
options.zh: 應避免舊量度方法，讓摺架任務感覺全新。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承接已有技巧並加應用，既不只重複，也不為新而丟棄有用方法。

speaking.en: We can build on the earlier work while adding a question it did not answer.
speaking.zh: 我們可承接早前工作，同時加入它未回答的問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再交代基礎與延伸。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區步行地圖已有清楚路線及地標，但輪椅使用者想知哪些段落有梯級。你負責回覆，不需重畫整張地圖，想沿用路線資料並新增實地核對的通行備註。用一至兩句英文提出更新。
writing.selfCheckZh: 明說沿用路線地標並新增實地通行核對，不把已有地圖當已無障礙核實，也不全盤重做。

examples.en: We can build on the existing route map by checking for steps and adding access notes. The clear landmarks can stay while we supply the missing practical information.
examples.zh: 我們可承接現有路線圖，查梯級並加通行備註；清楚地標可保留，同時補實際缺資料。

examples.en: Let us build on the route information rather than redraw everything. We should inspect each section and mark where a wheelchair user may need an alternative.
examples.zh: 承接路線資料，不用全重畫吧；應逐段視察，標明輪椅使用者可能需改道的位置。

takeaways.en: The discussion built on yesterday’s findings by asking what the new evidence changed.
takeaways.zh: 討論承接昨天發現，問新證據改變了甚麼。

takeaways.en: We want to build on the successful trial without assuming every detail will suit a larger group.
takeaways.zh: 我們想承接成功試行，但不假定每項細節都適合更大群體。

brief.meaningEn: Gradually, through many small contributions or steps.
brief.meaningZh: 透過許多小貢獻或步驟逐漸建立。
brief.grammar: build/rebuild/restore something brick by brick; identify the accumulated small actions.
brief.register: Established building metaphor. It highlights gradual construction, without necessarily prescribing a fixed sequence or promising success.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調小步累積，不只是拖慢，也不代表每步完全一樣或已有最後成果。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需有具體小動作及累積方向；一次大型改動本身不表達這種過程。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述持續累積的工作並保留實際進度。

listening.en: The volunteers rebuilt trust brick by brick, returning borrowed items on time and following up the small promises they made; attendance improved gradually rather than after one big announcement.
listening.zh: 義工準時歸還借物、跟進小承諾，一點一滴重建信任；出席逐步改善，不是在一次大宣布後突然改變。
listening.promptZh: brick by brick 強調甚麼？

options.en: Repeated small reliable actions gradually rebuilt trust.
options.zh: 反覆可靠小行動逐步重建信任。

options.en: A single announcement immediately restored the previous attendance.
options.zh: 一次宣布立即恢復原來出席。

options.en: The volunteers waited for trust to return without changing their actions.
options.zh: 義工不改行動，只等信任回來。

options.en: Attendance improved before the volunteers began keeping their promises.
options.zh: 義工開始守承諾前，出席已改善。

listening.explanationZh: 還物及跟進承諾是累積動作，與一次宣布或只等不同。

reply.promptZh: 義工怎樣逐步重建信任？
reply.promptEn: How did the volunteers rebuild trust?

options.en: They kept small promises and returned borrowed items on time.
options.zh: 他們守小承諾、準時還借物。

options.en: They rebuilt it brick by brick through reliable actions.
options.zh: 他們透過可靠行動一點一滴重建。

options.en: Their repeated follow-ups gave people reasons to trust them again.
options.zh: 反覆跟進讓大家有理由再信任。

options.en: They made gradual progress by doing the small things they said they would do.
options.zh: 他們做好答應的小事，逐步取得進展。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均給可靠小行動累積的過程。

scene.promptZh: 你把散亂家族紀錄每周整理一小批，查一點、補一點，半年後較有系統，尚未全完。哪句準確？

options.en: I am building the archive brick by brick through small weekly checks.
options.zh: 我透過每周小核對，一點一滴建立檔案。

options.en: One sorting session completed the whole archive.
options.zh: 一次整理完成整份檔案。

options.en: I have postponed checking the records until every missing detail arrives.
options.zh: 我延後核紀錄，直到每項缺資料都到齊。

scene.explanationZh: 每周小批累積，不是一次全完或先完全等候。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像 brick by brick？

options.en: Many small actions gradually establish something.
options.zh: 許多小動作逐漸建立某事。

options.en: A complete replacement happens in one move, with no gradual construction.
options.zh: 一次全面替換，沒有逐步建立過程。

options.en: Repeated contributions build up over time.
options.zh: 反覆貢獻隨時間累積。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次全換不展現小步累積。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想寫「一次宣布令出席全恢復」，但紀錄是多次履約後逐漸改善。哪句最好？

options.en: Describe the repeated actions and the gradual improvement rather than credit one announcement.
options.zh: 描述反覆行動及逐步改善，不歸功一次宣布。

options.en: The announcement is the clearest event, so we can treat it as the turning point without the follow-ups.
options.zh: 宣布是最清楚事件，可不提跟進就把它當轉捩點。

options.en: We should wait for full attendance before mentioning any progress.
options.zh: 應等全員出席後，才提任何進展。

dialogue.explanationZh: 逐步改善已有依據，可如實寫，不集中到單次宣布，也不需等完全恢復才承認。

speaking.en: We are building it brick by brick, and the small checks matter even though the work is not finished.
speaking.zh: 我們正一點一滴建立，工作未完，小核對仍有重要作用。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說小步累積。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你重新學鋼琴，朋友問為甚麼還未能彈完整新曲。你想說每天學兩小節、再接已會部分，曲目正一點一滴增加，目前只到半首；你也想邀他下周聽一次進度，不承諾到時必能全曲。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: I am building my repertoire brick by brick, learning two bars and joining them to the section I already know. I am halfway through this piece; would you like to hear my progress next week?
examples.zh: 我每天學兩小節、接已會部分，一點一滴建立曲目；這首目前到一半，你想下周聽進度嗎？

examples.en: The piece is coming together brick by brick through short daily practice, not one long session. I can play half of it now and would be glad to share the next stage with you.
examples.zh: 這首曲透過每天短練，一點一滴成形，不是一次長練；我現在可彈半首，也很樂意與你分享下一步。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用每天兩小節接已有段落交代技能與曲目累積，保留目前半首並邀分享進度，不以邀請保證下周完成。

takeaways.en: The collection grew brick by brick as residents contributed photographs and checked the captions.
takeaways.zh: 居民提供照片並核圖說，收藏一點一滴增長。

takeaways.en: They restored confidence brick by brick by keeping each small commitment.
takeaways.zh: 他們逐項守小承諾，一點一滴恢復信心。

brief.meaningEn: Perform essential underlying tasks correctly.
brief.meaningZh: 把必要的基本工作正確做好。
brief.grammar: get the basics right before adding complexity; getting/got the basics right; identify what the basics are in context.
brief.register: Natural evaluative phrase. What counts as basic depends on the task, not on a universal fixed checklist.
brief.boundaryZh: 基本做好不代表所有進階工作已完成，也不表示內容簡單所以不重要；需具體列要點。
brief.misconceptionZh: 加裝飾、增功能不能代替正確時間地點、材料或清楚指令等必要部分。
brief.outcomeZh: 能先辨認必要工作，再安排後續完善。

listening.en: Before adding animations to the event page, we needed to get the basics right: the date, the entrance and the booking link all had to be correct.
listening.zh: 活動頁加動畫前，我們需先做好基本工作：日期、入口及預約連結全要正確。
listening.promptZh: 基本工作在這裏指甚麼？

options.en: Correct event details and a working booking route before extra animation.
options.zh: 加動畫前，活動資料正確、預約途徑可用。

options.en: Completing the animation before checking the entrance.
options.zh: 核入口前先完成動畫。

options.en: Removing the booking link to keep the page visually simple.
options.zh: 為頁面外觀簡潔而刪預約連結。

options.en: Confirming that no design work will be needed after the date is correct.
options.zh: 確認日期正確後毋須任何設計工作。

listening.explanationZh: 已具體列日期入口連結，不是取消功能或排除之後設計。

reply.promptZh: 加動畫前，你們要先做甚麼？
reply.promptEn: What did you need to do before adding animations?

options.en: Check the date, entrance and booking link.
options.zh: 核日期、入口及預約連結。

options.en: Get the basics right so visitors can find and book the event.
options.zh: 先做好基本工作，讓訪客找到並預約活動。

options.en: Make sure the essential event information works before adding effects.
options.zh: 加效果前，確保必要活動資料可用。

options.en: Give people accurate practical details before polishing the presentation.
options.zh: 修飾呈現前，給大家準確實際資料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都列必要資訊或其實際用途。

scene.promptZh: 你為首次工作坊備漂亮講義，但材料數量未點、起步步驟未試；想先確保學生能開始。哪句貼切？

options.en: We need to get the basics right by checking the materials and trying the first steps.
options.zh: 我們需核材料、試起步步驟，先做好基本工作。

options.en: The polished handout is enough to show the materials and first steps are ready.
options.zh: 漂亮講義足以顯示材料和起步步驟都已準備好。

options.en: We should spend the remaining time on the cover before checking whether students can start.
options.zh: 應先用剩餘時間做封面，再查學生能否開始。

scene.explanationZh: 材料及起步是能開始的必要條件，封面不能代替。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 got the basics right 得出？

options.en: Essential tasks were handled correctly in context.
options.zh: 情境中的必要工作已正確處理。

options.en: Every advanced feature has also been completed.
options.zh: 每項進階功能也已完成。

options.en: The context should identify the underlying essentials.
options.zh: 情境應指出根本要點。

contrast.explanationZh: 基本正確不確立所有進階完成。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴覺得入口資料很簡單，想先跳過去做動畫，但訪客需靠它找門。哪句最好？

options.en: Its simplicity does not make it optional; let us confirm the entrance before adding effects.
options.zh: 簡單不代表可省；加效果前，先確認入口。

options.en: We can assume the entrance is unchanged and use the time for another effect.
options.zh: 可假定入口沒變，把時間加另一效果。

options.en: If entrance information is essential, we should remove the rest of the page design entirely.
options.zh: 若入口資料必要，應完全刪去其餘頁面設計。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先核必要資訊，不以簡單而跳過，也不需全棄設計。

speaking.en: We should get the basics right before adding details that cannot compensate for a missing essential.
speaking.zh: 加不能彌補缺失要點的細節前，我們應先做好基本工作。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指出具體必要工作。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替朋友管理借書交換，沒有核物主姓名便把一本書還錯人，現在想向物主道歉。你還未取回，會聯絡收錯書的人，並請物主一起確認書號及姓名才重排歸還。用一至兩句英文承認基本工作失誤及提出補救，不假裝已處理完。

examples.en: I did not get the basics right when I returned your book without checking the owner’s name, and I am sorry. I will contact the person who received it and confirm the book number with you before arranging its return.
examples.zh: 我未核物主姓名就還你的書，沒做好基本工作，對不起；我會聯絡收書者，與你確認書號後再排歸還。

examples.en: I should have got the basics right by matching the book number and the owner before handing it over. I apologise for the mistake and will ask you to check those details with me as I arrange to recover it.
examples.zh: 交書前，我應對上書號及物主，做好基本工作；我為錯誤道歉，安排取回時會請你一起核那些細節。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認未核姓名書號的基本失誤並道歉，安排聯絡及核實後取回，保留尚未追回，不把承諾當完成。

takeaways.en: The team got the basics right by confirming the meeting place and the start time.
takeaways.zh: 團隊確認集合地點及開始時間，做好基本工作。

takeaways.en: Getting the basics right helped the new volunteers begin without guessing what to do.
takeaways.zh: 做好基本工作，幫新義工開始時不用猜該做甚麼。

brief.meaningEn: Expand an operation with sound judgement about capacity and quality.
brief.meaningZh: 按能力及品質作審慎判斷，擴大運作規模。
brief.grammar: scale wisely as demand grows; scale here means expand an operation; wisely evaluates how it is managed, not a fixed technical method.
brief.register: Natural business and organisational wording, not a fixed idiom or promise of growth. The practical criteria should be explained.
brief.boundaryZh: 擴張需考慮人手、容量及品質，不表示越快越好或能保證成果；需具體說明判斷條件。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可先小範圍試增及核容量，不把需求增加直接當人手設備已足。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體條件說明審慎擴大，不只喊口號。

listening.en: The repair club wanted to scale wisely, so it trialled one extra session and checked whether volunteers could keep accurate records before promising a weekly programme at two venues.
listening.zh: 維修社想審慎擴大，所以先試加一場，核義工能否維持準確紀錄，才承諾兩場地每周活動。
listening.promptZh: 審慎擴大的具體做法是甚麼？

options.en: Trial a limited increase and check capacity before a wider commitment.
options.zh: 先有限度試增並核能力，再承諾更廣安排。

options.en: Promise both venues a weekly programme before testing the extra session.
options.zh: 試加場前，先承諾兩場地每周活動。

options.en: Treat demand alone as proof that the record-keeping capacity is sufficient.
options.zh: 只憑需求，便認定紀錄處理能力足夠。

options.en: Stop the existing programme in order to avoid any expansion decision.
options.zh: 為避免擴張決定，停止現有活動。

listening.explanationZh: 先一場試行及核紀錄能力，才考慮兩場地承諾。

reply.promptZh: 社團怎樣打算增加活動？
reply.promptEn: How does the club plan to increase its programme?

options.en: It will trial an extra session before making a wider weekly promise.
options.zh: 它會先試加一場，再作更廣每周承諾。

options.en: It wants to scale wisely by checking volunteer capacity during a limited trial.
options.zh: 它想在有限試行中核義工能力，審慎擴大。

options.en: The team will see whether accurate records can be maintained with the extra session.
options.zh: 團隊會看加場後能否維持準確紀錄。

options.en: A small increase will provide evidence before the two-venue plan is confirmed.
options.zh: 確認兩場地計劃前，小幅增加會提供依據。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給試行及核能力的實際方式。

scene.promptZh: 閱讀班等候名單變長，導師未試過更大班；你想先加一個試行小組，查看每人討論時間再決定。哪句貼切？

options.en: We can scale wisely by trialling another small group and checking the discussion time.
options.zh: 我們可先試加小組並核討論時間，審慎擴大。

options.en: The waiting list confirms that the same tutor can already manage a much larger class.
options.zh: 等候名單確認同一導師已可帶大得多的班。

options.en: We should promise places to everyone before checking how much discussion time remains.
options.zh: 應先答應所有人有位，再核討論時間剩多少。

scene.explanationZh: 需求不是教學容量證明，先試及核每人時間才有依據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像 scale wisely 的本課做法？

options.en: Testing a manageable increase before promising more.
options.zh: 承諾更多前先試可管理的增幅。

options.en: Expanding the commitment while leaving the capacity assumptions unchecked.
options.zh: 不核能力假設就擴大承諾。

options.en: Using evidence about quality and workload to guide the expansion.
options.zh: 用品質及工作量證據引導擴張。

contrast.explanationZh: 審慎需判斷能力及品質，不只是先承諾。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「報名多人就證明兩場地沒問題」，但還未試加場。哪句最好？

options.en: Demand tells us people are interested; the trial will tell us whether we can support the extra sessions.
options.zh: 需求說明有人有興趣；試行才讓我們知道能否支援加場。

options.en: The waiting list is enough to confirm that our present record system will cope.
options.zh: 等候名單足以確認目前紀錄系統能應付。

options.en: Let us confirm both venues now and use the first full week as the capacity check.
options.zh: 現在確認兩場地，用第一個完整周才核能力。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需求與供應能力不同，先有限度試行再作大承諾。

speaking.en: We want to scale wisely, using the trial to check what the team can support before promising more.
speaking.zh: 我們想審慎擴大，承諾更多前先用試行核團隊能支援甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說具體擴大條件。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你製作的地方歷史口述錄音受到另一區歡迎，對方想立即開放投稿；原有三人只能逐一核許可及字幕。你想提議先收一小批新區訪問、測核對所需時間，再決定常態接收量。用一至兩句英文回覆合作方。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把錄音收集轉化為可控投稿試行，核許可字幕時間後議月量；不以有興趣直接保證團隊容量。

examples.en: We would like to scale wisely by starting with a small batch of interviews from your district. That will show how much time our team needs to check permissions and subtitles before accepting regular submissions.
examples.zh: 我們想先收你區一小批訪問來審慎擴大；常態接稿前，可看團隊核許可及字幕需多少時間。

examples.en: To scale wisely, we should test the checking process with a few new recordings rather than open submissions immediately. Then we can agree on a manageable number each month.
examples.zh: 要審慎擴大，應先用幾段新錄音測核對流程，不立即開放投稿；之後可議每月可應付數量。

takeaways.en: The group scaled wisely by adding one location only after the trial showed it could maintain the service.
takeaways.zh: 試行顯示可維持服務後，小組才加一個地點，審慎擴大。

takeaways.en: We can scale wisely without assuming that a successful small session will run identically for a much larger group.
takeaways.zh: 我們可審慎擴大，不假定小場成功就會原樣適用大得多的群體。

titleEn: bite off more than you can chew

brief.meaningEn: Take on more work or responsibility than can be managed.
brief.meaningZh: 接下超出自己能應付的工作或責任。
brief.grammar: bite off more than you can chew; bit off more than I could chew; match the pronoun and tense to the person or organisation.
brief.register: Established eating metaphor, commonly critical or self-reflective. It concerns overcommitment, not necessarily lack of ability at each separate task.
brief.boundaryZh: 需看總量、時限及可用能力；不因新挑戰就必屬不自量力，也不表示當事人一項工作都不會做。
brief.misconceptionZh: 多項原本能做的任務也可能合起來超負荷；可縮範圍、改期或找支援。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出承諾超出甚麼能力及提出調整。

listening.en: I bit off more than I could chew by promising to edit the booklet and organise the exhibition in the same week; I knew both tasks separately, but I had not allowed enough time for them together.
listening.zh: 我答應同一周編小冊又辦展覽，接下超出能應付的工作；兩件事分別我都熟悉，但沒為一起做留足時間。
listening.promptZh: 超負荷的原因是甚麼？

options.en: Two familiar tasks were promised together without enough time.
options.zh: 兩項熟悉任務一起答應，時間卻不足。

options.en: The speaker had no experience of either task individually.
options.zh: 說話者個別做兩項任務都沒有經驗。

options.en: The exhibition was cancelled before the editing was promised.
options.zh: 答應編輯前，展覽已取消。

options.en: The tasks were completed early because their schedules did not overlap.
options.zh: 兩項時間沒重疊，所以提早完成。

listening.explanationZh: 分別熟悉不等於同周容量足；說話者承諾總量超時。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說自己接得太多？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say you took on too much?

options.en: I had promised two demanding tasks for the same week without enough time.
options.zh: 我同一周答應兩項需投入任務，時間不足。

options.en: I bit off more than I could chew by taking on both at once.
options.zh: 我同時接兩項，超出能應付的量。

options.en: Knowing each task did not give me enough hours to manage them together.
options.zh: 熟悉每項工作，不會讓我有足夠時數一起完成。

options.en: The combined workload was larger than the time I had available.
options.zh: 合起來的工作量超出可用時間。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出總量與時間不匹配，不否定單項能力。

scene.promptZh: 你一周只可投入兩個晚上，卻答應教三班及為每班個別改稿，發現無法按時回覆。哪句準確？

options.en: I have bitten off more than I can chew with this teaching and feedback schedule.
options.zh: 這教學與回饋時間表令我接了超出能應付的工作。

options.en: The late replies show that I cannot teach any individual class.
options.zh: 遲回覆顯示我連任何一班都不會教。

options.en: The schedule fits comfortably into my two available evenings.
options.zh: 時間表很輕鬆便可放入我兩個可用晚上。

scene.explanationZh: 承諾總量超出兩晚，不等於單班能力全無。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 bite off more than you can chew？

options.en: Several commitments exceed the time and support available.
options.zh: 幾項承諾超出可用時間及支援。

options.en: A demanding new task fits the agreed capacity and is being managed as planned.
options.zh: 有要求的新任務符合議定能力，正按計劃處理。

options.en: Someone agrees to more work than they can realistically deliver.
options.zh: 某人答應超出實際可交付的工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 新而難未必超負荷，需有承諾超能力的依據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「你會編小冊，也會辦展覽，怎會太多？」但兩項同周已排滿。哪句最好？

options.en: I can do each separately, but the combined deadline needs more time than I have.
options.zh: 我分別會做，但合起來的限期需比我現有更多時間。

options.en: Then knowing both methods means I should keep both deadlines unchanged.
options.zh: 既然懂兩種方法，我就應保持兩個限期不變。

options.en: If I cannot do them together, I should stop offering either service in future.
options.zh: 若不能一起做，我以後就應停止提供任何一項服務。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需評總量及時間，並非懂方法便無限容量，或一次超負荷就永遠不能做。

speaking.en: I bit off more than I could chew, so I need to reduce the scope or agree on more time.
speaking.zh: 我接了超出能應付的工作，所以需縮範圍或議多點時間。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明過度承諾及調整。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你原答應家庭聚會做一道主菜，後來又自告奮勇做四款甜品及布置場地，當天只得一個早上。你想及早告訴家人自己接得太多，保留主菜、請別人接甜品，不是說自己不會煮飯。用一至兩句英文求調整。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出新增多項與一早時間不符，及早請分甜品並保留主菜責任，不把超總量當完全不會煮。

examples.en: I have bitten off more than I can chew by adding four desserts and the decorations to the main dish. Could I keep the main dish and ask others to take over the desserts?
examples.zh: 我在主菜外加四款甜品及布置，接了超出能應付的工作；可否保留主菜，請別人接甜品？

examples.en: I bit off more than I could chew for one morning, even though I can cook these dishes separately. Let us share the desserts so I can finish the main dish properly.
examples.zh: 雖然我分別會煮這些菜，一個早上卻接了太多；分擔甜品，讓我好好完成主菜吧。

takeaways.en: The team bit off more than it could chew when it promised three launches in the same month.
takeaways.zh: 團隊答應同月推出三項服務時，接了超出能應付的工作。

takeaways.en: She realised she was biting off more than she could chew and asked to narrow the assignment.
takeaways.zh: 她發現自己正接下超出能應付的工作，便要求縮小任務範圍。

brief.meaningEn: Fail or collapse suddenly and dramatically.
brief.meaningZh: 突然且大幅地失敗或崩潰。
brief.grammar: a plan/hope comes crashing down; came crashing down in past; identify the dependency or event that triggers the collapse.
brief.register: Emphatic collapse image, figurative here. Stronger than a minor setback or routine revision.
brief.boundaryZh: 需有明顯整體崩潰，而非小幅延誤；不由一次失敗推所有往後都無可能。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可描寫某計劃崩潰並另想後續，不把它與永久失去任何機會混淆。
brief.outcomeZh: 能選合適強度描述突發失敗及其具體影響。

listening.en: Our plan came crashing down when the only driver withdrew the night before the trip: without another approved driver, we could not take the group out as arranged.
listening.zh: 唯一司機在旅行前夜退出時，我們的計劃突然崩潰；沒有另一位獲批准司機，就不能按安排帶小組外出。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼使這次計劃突然無法照辦？

options.en: The essential driver withdrew and no approved replacement was available.
options.zh: 必要司機退出，沒有獲批准替補。

options.en: A small change to the route left the trip otherwise ready to proceed.
options.zh: 路線稍改，其餘仍可照行。

options.en: The team found a replacement driver before the withdrawal affected the plan.
options.zh: 退出未影響計劃前，團隊已找到替補。

options.en: The group decided never to arrange another outing.
options.zh: 小組決定永不再辦外出。

listening.explanationZh: 唯一司機退出造成這次安排不能照辦，未說永久停辦。

reply.promptZh: 旅行計劃為甚麼突然無法照辦？
reply.promptEn: Why did the trip plan suddenly become impossible to carry out?

options.en: The only driver withdrew and we had no approved replacement.
options.zh: 唯一司機退出，我們沒有獲批准替補。

options.en: It came crashing down when the essential transport arrangement fell through.
options.zh: 必要交通安排落空時，計劃突然崩潰。

options.en: Without a driver, the group could not travel as arranged.
options.zh: 沒有司機，小組無法按安排出行。

options.en: A key requirement disappeared too late for us to replace it.
options.zh: 關鍵條件太遲才失去，我們來不及替補。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給必要交通條件失去的原因。

scene.promptZh: 你答應按時直播演出，唯一供電系統開始前故障，當晚無替補，整場不能播；之後仍可另排錄影。哪句準確？

options.en: The live-stream plan came crashing down when the power system failed.
options.zh: 供電系統故障時，直播計劃突然崩潰。

options.en: A minor delay left the live stream running as planned that evening.
options.zh: 小延誤後，當晚直播仍按計劃進行。

options.en: The later recording proves the live stream was completed that night.
options.zh: 之後錄影證明當晚已完成直播。

scene.explanationZh: 當晚整場不能播支持強烈崩潰；另排錄影不改當晚結果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜用 come crashing down 形容？

options.en: The sole essential arrangement fails and the plan cannot proceed.
options.zh: 唯一必要安排失敗，計劃不能進行。

options.en: A small wording correction is made while the project continues normally.
options.zh: 作一點措辭修正，項目仍正常進行。

options.en: An unexpected loss brings an elaborate scheme to a sudden end.
options.zh: 意外失去條件，令複雜方案突然結束。

contrast.explanationZh: 普通小修不需用崩潰的強度。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因這次旅行辦不成，就宣布小組永遠不能再外出；你只知當晚沒替補。哪句最好？

options.en: This plan collapsed, but a later outing would depend on making new arrangements.
options.zh: 這次計劃崩潰，但以後外出要看能否作新安排。

options.en: The failed trip is enough to rule out every future outing.
options.zh: 這次失敗足以排除以後所有外出。

options.en: We can announce a confirmed outing next week before checking whether another driver is available.
options.zh: 未查另一司機能否來，就可宣布下周已確認外出。

dialogue.explanationZh: 這次安排已失敗，但未確立永遠不能外出；日後能否辦需另核司機及安排，不能提前宣布已定。

speaking.en: The plan came crashing down when we lost the one arrangement it depended on.
speaking.zh: 失去唯一依賴的安排時，計劃突然崩潰。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再用合適強度描述計劃失敗。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫短篇故事，角色打算會見持有唯一證據副本的人，取回副本並在當天揭露真相；到門口才發現對方已帶副本離城，當天計劃全落空。角色仍想另尋證人。用一至兩句英文寫這轉折，不寫成只晚幾分鐘。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用關鍵副本及持有人離開造成當天揭證全落空，接另找證人的下一步；不是小延誤或永久無望。

examples.en: Her plan came crashing down when she learned that the person holding the only copy had left town. She would have to look for another witness rather than reveal the evidence that day.
examples.zh: 得知持唯一副本的人已離城，她的計劃突然崩潰；她需另找證人，不能當天揭證。

examples.en: The plan to expose the truth that afternoon came crashing down at the doorway. With the only copy gone, she began thinking about who else might have seen what happened.
examples.zh: 當天下午揭真相的計劃在門口突然崩潰；唯一副本不在，她開始想還有誰可能見過事件。

takeaways.en: Their hopes came crashing down when they learned there was no place for them on the course.
takeaways.zh: 得知課程沒有他們的名額時，他們的希望突然破滅。

takeaways.en: The scheme came crashing down after the central agreement was withdrawn.
takeaways.zh: 核心協議撤回後，方案突然崩潰。
